articles.title: TopEdge Documentation
articles.description: Guides and reference for running WhatsApp automation on Shopify with TopEdge — setup, journeys, cart recovery, COD confirmation, templates and billing.
articles.lead: Everything the dashboard does, written for the person running the store. Start with the [quickstart](/docs/quickstart) if you just signed up, or jump to a screen in [Reference](/docs/reference/journeys).

faqs.question: Do I need the WhatsApp Business app to use TopEdge?
faqs.answer: No. TopEdge runs on the WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API), which is a different product from the WhatsApp Business phone app. You can keep using the app on a different number, or enable coexistence on the same number if your WhatsApp Business Account supports it.

faqs.question: Can I use TopEdge without Shopify?
faqs.answer: The inbox, Flow Builder, templates, campaigns and the AI brain all work without Shopify. Order journeys, cart recovery, product catalogue and store economics need the Shopify connection, because those read order and checkout data from your store.

faqs.question: How long does setup take?
faqs.answer: Connecting Shopify and WhatsApp takes about 30 minutes if you already have a WhatsApp Business Account on Meta. The variable is template approval — Meta usually reviews in minutes, but a first submission can take up to 24 hours.

blocks.text: TopEdge connects your Shopify store to the WhatsApp Cloud API. Order updates, COD confirmations and abandoned-cart recovery then send on their own, and every reply lands in one shared inbox. To start, connect Shopify and WhatsApp and get your message templates approved by Meta.
How the pieces fit together
**Shopify owns orders, WhatsApp owns messaging, and Journeys connect the two.** Everything else in the dashboard is a view on top of those three.

articles.title: Quickstart: WhatsApp automation for Shopify
articles.description: Go live with TopEdge in about 30 minutes: connect Shopify and WhatsApp, approve an order template, publish one journey and send yourself a test message.
articles.lead: The shortest path from a new workspace to a real WhatsApp message about a real order. Roughly 30 minutes of work, plus however long Meta takes to approve your first template.

faqs.question: Why has my test WhatsApp message not arrived?
faqs.answer: Check four things in order: the journey is Published rather than Draft, the template it uses shows Approved, the order carries a phone number in international format, and WhatsApp still shows Connected. The order detail page records a skip reason that names which of these failed.

faqs.question: Can I test without placing a real order?
faqs.answer: Yes for conversations — Flow Builder has a simulator that walks menus and buttons without messaging anyone. Order journeys need a real Shopify order to trigger, so most merchants place a small test order and cancel or refund it afterwards.

faqs.question: Do I need a new phone number for WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but the number cannot be actively registered in the WhatsApp Business app unless your WhatsApp Business Account has coexistence enabled. Many merchants use a dedicated number for automation and keep their existing one for manual chats.

blocks.text: To go live, connect Shopify and WhatsApp, then submit one order-confirmation template to Meta. Once it is approved, publish the order-placed journey and place a test order on your own phone. Cart recovery, campaigns and the AI brain all build on that base.

items: Shopify admin access to the store you want to connect.
A WhatsApp Business Account on the Cloud API, with a phone number that is **not** currently active in the WhatsApp Business app (or with coexistence enabled).
Admin rights in Meta Business Manager, so you can approve the connection and submit templates.
A second phone you can message from — a business number cannot message itself.

steps.body: **Settings → WhatsApp → Connect** and run Meta's embedded signup. Approve the WhatsApp Business Account and phone number TopEdge should send from.

steps.body: Open **Orders** and press **Sync**. Real orders appear within a minute or two; if the table stays empty, re-approve your Shopify permissions.

steps.body: Open **Journeys → Order placed** and map the WhatsApp step to your approved template. Press **Publish**; draft journeys send nothing.

steps.body: Check out on your own store with your own phone number. The WhatsApp confirmation should arrive within seconds, and the order detail page logs the send.

articles.title: Connect WhatsApp Cloud API to TopEdge
articles.description: Connect your WhatsApp Business Account to TopEdge: embedded Meta signup, the messages webhook, permanent access tokens, and how to fix a disconnected channel.
articles.lead: TopEdge sends and receives on the WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API). This page covers the connection, the webhook that makes the inbox work, and what to do when the channel drops.

faqs.question: Why is my WhatsApp inbox empty even though the channel is connected?
faqs.answer: Connection and the message subscription are separate. TopEdge can send as soon as the token is valid, but replies only arrive once TopEdge is subscribed to your messages. Embedded signup does this for you; if the inbox stays empty, reconnect from Settings → WhatsApp.

faqs.question: What kind of WhatsApp access token should I use?
faqs.answer: A System User token with the whatsapp_business_messaging permission. The token offered on the Meta developer dashboard is a temporary test token that expires in roughly 24 hours, which makes the channel appear to break by itself the next day.

faqs.question: Can I keep using the WhatsApp Business app on the same number?
faqs.answer: Only if coexistence is enabled on your WhatsApp Business Account. Otherwise a number can be registered either on the Cloud API or in the WhatsApp Business app, not both, and embedded signup will report that the number is already in use.

blocks.text: Connect from **Settings → WhatsApp** using Meta's embedded signup. It creates the access token and subscribes TopEdge to your messages for you. Send yourself a test message afterwards to confirm replies reach the inbox.

items: A WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) in Meta Business Manager, and admin rights on it.
A phone number that can receive an SMS or call to verify, and that is not actively registered in the WhatsApp Business app.
A verified business on Meta if you want to raise your messaging limits beyond the starting tier.

blocks.text: Connect with embedded signup (recommended)

blocks.alt: Settings channels list with the WhatsApp card and its Connect button

blocks.text: Embedded signup runs Meta’s own flow inside the dashboard, so you never handle a token yourself. In one pass it:

items: **Creates or selects** your WhatsApp Business Account (WABA).
**Registers** the phone number.
**Subscribes** TopEdge to the account.
**Stores** a long-lived access token.

blocks.howToName: Connect a WhatsApp Business Account to TopEdge

steps.title: Open WhatsApp connections
steps.body: Settings → WhatsApp → **Connect**.

steps.title: Sign in to Meta
steps.body: Use the Facebook account that administers your business. A personal account with no Business Manager access cannot finish this.

steps.title: Pick or create the WhatsApp Business Account
steps.body: Choose the WABA that owns the number you want to send from. A second WABA for the same business is a common reason templates later seem to go missing.

steps.title: Add and verify the phone number
steps.body: Enter the number, choose SMS or voice, and type the code. Verified numbers show green in Meta.

steps.title: Finish and return to TopEdge
steps.body: The card should read **Connected**, with the phone number and WhatsApp Business Account it uses.

steps.title: Send yourself a test
steps.body: Message your business number from a personal phone. The thread should appear in Live Chat within seconds.
steps.note: Embedded signup subscribes TopEdge to your messages, so there is no webhook to set up.

blocks.text: Manual credentials (advanced)
Manual credentials are hidden in the dashboard and only needed when embedded signup cannot finish, for example on an agency-managed WABA.
**Contact TopEdge support** to switch it on. You will need four values from the Meta developer console: the Phone Number ID, the WABA ID, an access token and your Meta App ID.

blocks.title: Temporary tokens expire in about 24 hours
blocks.body: The token on the Meta developer dashboard is a test token, so a channel that dies after a day almost always used one. Production needs a **System User** token with the `whatsapp_business_messaging` permission, which does not expire.

items.definition: Identifies the specific number messages send from. Not the phone number itself — a numeric ID from Meta.
The account that owns your numbers and templates. Templates are scoped to this, which is why connecting the wrong WABA makes your template library look empty.
Authorises TopEdge to call Meta on your behalf. Use a System User token in production.
A shared secret Meta echoes back when it first calls your webhook URL, proving the endpoint is yours.

items: The WhatsApp card reads **Connected** with the right phone number.
No amber "WhatsApp disconnected" bar at the top of the dashboard.
A test message from a personal phone lands in Live Chat.

blocks.text: If something goes wrong

cases.symptom: Amber "WhatsApp disconnected" bar across every page
fixes: Open Settings → WhatsApp and reconnect. If you are on manual credentials, paste a fresh permanent System User token.
A token that stopped working overnight was almost certainly a 24-hour test token.
Confirm the number has not been disconnected or migrated inside Meta Business Manager.
Reconnect, then send a test message to confirm inbound still arrives.

cases.symptom: Connection succeeds but the inbox stays empty
fixes: Reconnect from Settings → WhatsApp so embedded signup re-subscribes TopEdge to your messages. Sending works without it, receiving does not.
Message from a personal phone. A business number cannot message itself.
Confirm a flow is Published in [Flow Builder](/docs/reference/flow-builder), otherwise inbound messages arrive with no automated reply.

cases.symptom: Embedded signup says the phone number is already in use
fixes: The number is registered in the WhatsApp Business app. Either delete that account or enable coexistence on your WABA.
Check for a second Cloud API app already claiming the number in Meta Business Manager.
As a last resort, verify a different number and keep the old one for manual chats.

cases.symptom: Template library is empty after connecting
fixes: You are almost certainly connected to a different WhatsApp Business Account than the one holding your templates.
Check which WABA the connection names, and compare it with the account in Meta Business Manager.
Reconnect against the correct WABA, then use **Sync from Meta** in Meta Manager.

articles.title: Connect Shopify to TopEdge
articles.description: Install the TopEdge Shopify app, understand the permissions it asks for, verify that orders sync, and fix a store stuck on Reconnect.
articles.lead: The Shopify connection powers order journeys, cart recovery, the product catalogue and store economics. It is an app install, so the flow always starts and finishes in Shopify admin.

faqs.question: Does TopEdge edit my Shopify theme?
faqs.answer: No. Storefront tracking installs through Shopify app embeds and the web pixel extension, both of which are managed in the theme editor and removed cleanly when you disable them. TopEdge reads your theme only to check whether the opt-in embed is enabled.

faqs.question: Why does Shopify ask me to reconnect?
faqs.answer: Shopify requires a fresh approval whenever an app starts using a capability you have not already granted. Until you approve it, the features relying on that capability stop working — missing shipped and delivered messages are the usual symptom.

faqs.question: Can I connect more than one Shopify store?
faqs.answer: Each workspace binds to one Shopify store, so a second store needs its own workspace. Connecting a different store to an existing workspace releases the previous binding, which is why test stores should be disconnected before you connect the real one.

blocks.text: Connect from **Settings → Shopify**, or open TopEdge from Shopify admin. You approve the app’s permissions once in Shopify, and orders start syncing within a minute or two. You never type your store domain; the install is always approved inside Shopify.

items: Shopify admin or staff access with permission to install apps.
A store on a plan that allows app installs (development stores are fine for testing).
If you also use a third-party checkout, access to that provider’s dashboard for the webhook step.

blocks.text: Install the app

blocks.alt: Shopify connect window showing the connected store and its list of approved permissions

blocks.howToName: Connect a Shopify store to TopEdge

steps.title: Start the connect flow
steps.body: **Settings → Shopify → Connect**. You can also start from **Shopify admin → Apps → TopEdge**, which brings you back to the dashboard afterwards.

steps.title: Approve the permissions in Shopify
steps.body: Shopify shows the full permission list. Approve all of it, because a partial grant breaks specific features silently instead of disabling them visibly.
steps.note: See [what each permission is for](#permissions) below.

steps.title: Wait for webhooks to register
steps.body: TopEdge subscribes to the order, fulfilment, checkout and app-lifecycle webhooks it needs. This happens automatically right after install.

steps.title: Verify orders sync
steps.body: Open **Orders** and press **Sync**. Live orders should appear within one to two minutes.

steps.title: Install storefront tracking
steps.body: Only needed for cart recovery and browse events. **Store growth → Website tracking** installs the theme embed, web pixel and checkout extension; see [Store growth](/docs/reference/store-growth).

blocks.alt: Orders table listing real Shopify orders after a sync
blocks.caption: After a Sync, Orders lists your real store orders.

blocks.text: What the permissions are for

Shopify asks you to approve everything at once, so here is what each group unlocks. TopEdge writes to your store only for the actions listed, such as tagging an order, setting stock or creating a payment link.

rows: Order journeys and triggers, commerce analytics, and the order actions you take from the inbox — tag, cancel, mark paid.
Product catalogue for flows and message templates, stock levels, and setting quantities from the Stock screen.
Audience CRM, identity matching by phone number, and abandoned checkout detection for cart recovery.
Shipped and delivered journeys, tracking numbers, and creating fulfilments from the Orders screen.
COD → prepaid payment links and cart recovery invoices, plus issuing recovery discount codes.
The storefront web pixel that captures carts and browse events.
Detecting whether the TopEdge opt-in app embed is enabled on your live theme. TopEdge never edits theme files.
Session and payout figures shown in Insights. Read-only, and never used to move money.

blocks.title: Permissions change over time
blocks.body: When the app starts using a new Shopify capability, your store shows a **Reconnect** prompt. Approving it re-grants the full set; until then the new feature stays off, which is why something can seem to stop after an update.

items: The Shopify card reads **Connected** and shows your store domain.
Orders lists real orders after a Sync.
Product search returns your catalogue.
For cart recovery: every layer on Store growth → Website tracking is green.

blocks.text: If something goes wrong

cases.symptom: Shopify card shows Reconnect, or fulfilments are missing
fixes: Settings → Shopify → **Reconnect** and approve the full permission list again.
Open Orders → **Sync** and wait a couple of minutes.
Missing shipped or delivered messages are nearly always missing fulfilment permissions — reconnecting fixes it.

cases.symptom: Orders table stays empty after connecting
fixes: Press **Sync** on the Orders screen; the first load is a backfill, not a webhook.
Confirm the connected store domain is the store you are actually looking at in Shopify admin.
If you connected several stores while testing, make sure this workspace owns the right one.

cases.symptom: Dashboard numbers do not match Shopify analytics
fixes: Compare the same date range and the same definition — Shopify’s total sales includes shipping and tax, while store economics reports net of cost.
Press Sync to backfill any orders that arrived while the connection was down.
Orders placed before you connected are backfilled, but only for the window the sync covers.

cases.symptom: You uninstalled from Shopify but TopEdge still shows Connected
fixes: Reload the dashboard — connection state is cached briefly.
If it persists, press Reconnect and then disconnect cleanly from Settings.
Uninstalling in Shopify revokes the token, so no further data moves either way regardless of what the card says.

articles.title: Go-live checklist before real customers
articles.description: The checks to run before TopEdge messages real customers: connections, approved templates, published journeys, consent, tracking and a live end-to-end test.
articles.lead: Work down this list once before launch. Every item has caused a real merchant either silence where a message should have been, or a message that should not have gone out.

faqs.question: What is the most common reason a WhatsApp automation does not send?
faqs.answer: A journey left in Draft. Publishing is a separate action from saving, and a saved draft looks complete in the editor while sending nothing. The second most common reason is a template that is still pending Meta approval.

faqs.question: Do order confirmations need marketing consent?
faqs.answer: No. Order, shipping and delivery updates are transactional and send as Utility templates, which do not require marketing opt-in. Promotional broadcasts are different and do need recorded consent from the contact.

blocks.text: Before going live, confirm both channels are connected and every template your journeys use is **Approved**. Each journey you expect to run must be **Published**, and marketing should target only contacts with recorded consent. Then run one real end-to-end test on a real phone.
Connections

blocks.alt: Settings with the WhatsApp and Shopify cards showing their connection state

items: Shopify shows **Connected** with the correct store domain.
WhatsApp shows **Connected** with the number you want customers to see.
A test message from your phone shows up in Live Chat.
Your WhatsApp token is a permanent System User token, not a 24-hour test token.
Gmail is connected if any journey or campaign sends email.

blocks.text: Templates

blocks.alt: Meta Manager template library listing templates with their approval status

items: Every template referenced by a published journey shows **Approved**.
Order and shipping templates are in the **Utility** category and contain no promotional language.
Promotional templates are in the **Marketing** category.
Variables are mapped — a template with unmapped variables sends with blanks or fails outright.
The preview in the dashboard matches what you want the customer to receive.

blocks.title: Approved at send time, not at publish time
blocks.body: Meta can pause or disable a template after approval if quality drops. A journey that worked last week can then start skipping sends with no change on your side; the skip reason on the order says so.

blocks.text: Automations

blocks.alt: Journeys hub listing order and cart automations

items: Each journey you expect to run shows **Published**. Draft journeys never send.
The trigger on each journey matches the event you think it does — order confirmation is the **order placed** trigger.
Trigger filters are deliberate. All rules combine with AND, so two narrow rules can exclude everyone.
Wait timings are what you intend — the first cart reminder is minutes, not instant.
Your main flow is Published in Flow Builder, so replies get an answer.

blocks.text: Consent and compliance

items: Marketing broadcasts target only contacts with recorded opt-in.
No purchased or scraped phone lists are loaded into Audience.
Opt-in tools carry consent wording that names WhatsApp marketing explicitly.
STOP handling is understood — it opts the contact out of marketing automatically.
Order and shipping updates use Utility templates, which do not require marketing consent.

blocks.title: Where consent can legitimately come from
blocks.caption: Each source records how the contact opted in, which is what you rely on if Meta ever asks.

blocks.text: Tracking (for cart recovery only)

items: All three layers on Store growth → Website tracking are green.
The TopEdge opt-in app embed is enabled on your **live** theme, not a preview theme.
A test abandoned checkout produced a cart row **with a phone number**.
If you use a third-party checkout, its webhook is configured and tested.

steps.title: Place a real order on your own phone
steps.body: Use a number you control, in international format. Check the WhatsApp message reads correctly on the phone, not just in the dashboard preview.

steps.title: Abandon a checkout
steps.body: Enter your phone at checkout and leave. Confirm the cart shows under abandoned carts with the phone filled in, then wait for the first reminder.

steps.title: Reply to the message
steps.body: Your reply should appear in Live Chat and trigger your welcome flow. This proves the webhook works inbound too.

steps.title: Reply yourself, then give it back
steps.body: Press **Reply myself** on the thread and send a free-form reply. Then press **Give back to bot** and confirm automation resumes on your next message.

steps.title: Check the money
steps.body: Complete the abandoned checkout. Confirm the cart is marked recovered with revenue attributed.

articles.title: Set up WhatsApp abandoned cart recovery
articles.description: Capture the phone number at checkout, publish a three-message cart recovery journey on WhatsApp, and read recovered revenue instead of vanity send counts.
articles.lead: Cart recovery has two halves that fail on their own: capturing a phone number at checkout, and sending an approved template afterwards. Get capture working first, because a perfect journey sends nothing to a cart with no phone number.

faqs.question: How soon should the first abandoned cart message go out?
faqs.answer: Around 25 to 30 minutes after abandonment. Sending instantly annoys customers who simply switched tabs, and waiting several hours loses the people who were still deciding. The default capture delay is 25 minutes and most stores never need to change it.

faqs.question: Why is my abandoned cart missing a phone number?
faqs.answer: Because the customer left before reaching a step that collects one, or because the checkout extension is not capturing. Adding to cart alone never produces a phone number. Check that all three tracking layers are green and that the TopEdge app embed is enabled on your live theme.

faqs.question: How many cart recovery messages should I send?
faqs.answer: Three is the standard ladder: a reminder, an objection-handling message, and a final nudge. More than three starts costing you more in conversation fees and goodwill than it recovers, and it raises your chance of being blocked or reported.

faqs.question: Does cart recovery need marketing opt-in?
faqs.answer: Cart recovery templates are reviewed by Meta like any other template, and promotional framing belongs in the Marketing category, which does require consent. Keep the ladder transactional in tone and treat consent as a requirement whenever a message carries an offer.

blocks.text: Install the three storefront tracking layers so abandoned checkouts arrive with a phone number, and get three cart-recovery templates approved. Then publish a journey on the **cart abandoned** trigger with waits of about 25 minutes, 6 hours and 24 hours. Recovered revenue is credited on last touch within seven days.

items: Shopify and WhatsApp both connected — [Connect Shopify](/docs/connect-shopify), [Connect WhatsApp](/docs/connect-whatsapp).
Storefront tracking installed and green — [Store growth](/docs/reference/store-growth).
Three cart-recovery templates Approved in [Meta Manager](/docs/reference/meta-manager).
A test product you can add to cart and abandon.

blocks.text: How recovery actually works

steps.title: Customer leaves checkout
steps.body: Shopify records an abandoned checkout, and TopEdge saves it as a cart lead.

steps.title: The lead is enrolled
steps.body: A scheduler finds your live cart journeys and enrols the lead. Each wait in the journey becomes a scheduled send.

steps.title: The customer orders
steps.body: If they order at any point, the remaining steps cancel and the cart is marked recovered.

blocks.name: cart-recovery-ladder
blocks.title: The default three-message ladder
blocks.caption: The first reminder is deliberately not instant — a customer who stepped away for two minutes does not need chasing.

blocks.title: No phone number means no recovery
blocks.body: Adding to cart is not enough: the customer must reach a step that captures a phone number or email. If the phone column on a cart row is blank, fix tracking, not the journey.

blocks.text: Step 1 — get the phone number

blocks.alt: Store growth → Website tracking with a health row for the theme embed, web pixel and checkout extension

blocks.name: tracking-layers
blocks.title: All three layers have to be healthy
blocks.caption: The checkout extension is the one that captures the phone number, so a green theme embed alone will not produce recoverable carts.

blocks.howToName: Capture abandoned checkout phone numbers on Shopify

steps.title: Open website tracking
steps.body: **Store growth → Website tracking**. You should see one health row per layer.

steps.title: Install each layer
steps.body: Use one-click install for the theme app embed, the web pixel and the checkout extension. Each must report green.

steps.title: Enable the app embed on your live theme
steps.body: **Shopify admin → Online Store → Themes → Customize** on the **live** theme → **App embeds** → enable the TopEdge embeds → **Save**.
steps.note: A preview theme does not count. This is the most common reason tracking looks installed but captures nothing.

steps.title: Run a test abandonment
steps.body: In an incognito window, add to cart and reach checkout. Enter a real phone number, then close the tab without paying.

steps.title: Confirm the cart row
steps.body: Open **Store growth → Abandoned carts**. Within a few minutes a row should appear **with the phone number filled in**.

blocks.alt: Abandoned carts list with phone numbers, cart values and recovery stats
blocks.caption: A healthy setup shows carts with the phone column filled in.

blocks.text: If you use a third-party checkout
One-page and COD-optimised checkouts replace Shopify’s native checkout, so the checkout extension never runs.

articles.title: Confirm COD orders on WhatsApp to cut RTO
articles.description: Confirm cash-on-delivery orders over WhatsApp with button replies, cancel the ones nobody confirms, and offer a prepaid switch to reduce return-to-origin losses.
articles.h1: COD confirmation and the prepaid switch
articles.lead: Return-to-origin (RTO) is the most expensive problem in Indian D2C, and most of it is decided before dispatch. A two-button confirmation sent minutes after the order separates the customers who meant it from the ones who did not.

faqs.question: Does WhatsApp COD confirmation actually reduce RTO?
faqs.answer: It reduces the share of RTO caused by unintended and duplicate orders, which is the largest removable chunk. It cannot fix RTO caused by delivery failures, wrong addresses or buyer remorse after dispatch. Measure your own before-and-after rather than trusting a headline number.

faqs.question: When should the COD confirmation message be sent?
faqs.answer: Five to fifteen minutes after the order. The customer still remembers placing it, and you are well ahead of dispatch. Sending instantly feels automated and jumpy; waiting hours means the order may already be packed.

faqs.question: What should I do when a customer never confirms?
faqs.answer: Send exactly one follow-up, then apply your own rule. Many stores hold high-value unconfirmed COD orders for a phone call and dispatch low-value ones anyway, because the shipping cost of being wrong is smaller than the lost sale.

faqs.question: Do I need a separate template for COD confirmation?
faqs.answer: Yes. It needs quick-reply buttons so the customer can answer with one tap, and the body has to read as a transactional order confirmation to pass review as a Utility template. Your order confirmation template will not have the buttons.

blocks.text: Publish a journey on the **order placed** trigger, filtered to COD, that sends an approved template with Confirm and Cancel buttons within minutes. Confirmed orders go to dispatch and silent ones get one follow-up. On Growth plans and above you can also offer a prepaid payment link that replaces the COD order with a paid one.

items: Shopify and WhatsApp connected, with orders syncing.
An approved template with quick-reply buttons — see [Message templates](/docs/platform/message-templates).
For the prepaid switch: a plan that includes COD → prepaid, and Shopify permission to create draft orders.
A COD order you can place as a test.

blocks.text: Why confirmation works
A COD order costs nothing to place, so it attracts impulse, duplicate and mistaken orders. You usually find out at the door, after paying for shipping both ways.
One tap of confirmation moves that discovery to before dispatch, where cancelling is almost free.

rows: Dispatch normally. Tag the order as confirmed so your warehouse can see it.
Cancel in Shopify before dispatch. You just saved both legs of shipping.
The thread is in [Live Chat](/docs/reference/live-chat) with the order beside it — answer and confirm manually.
Send one follow-up. After that, decide by your own risk rules: hold, call, or dispatch anyway.

steps.title: Create a journey on order placed
steps.body: **Journeys → New**, trigger **Order placed**. Order confirmation *is* the order-placed trigger; there is no separate "order confirmed" event.
steps.note: This is the single most common point of confusion when building this journey.

steps.title: Filter to COD only
steps.body: In the trigger setup, add a **payment method** rule set to COD. Without it, prepaid customers are asked to confirm orders they already paid for.

steps.title: Add a short wait
steps.body: Five to fifteen minutes. The customer has left your site, but the message is clearly about the order they just placed.

steps.title: Send the confirmation template
steps.body: Map an approved template with Confirm and Cancel quick replies. TopEdge sets the step to wait for a button tap rather than free text.

steps.title: Branch on the answer (Growth and above)
steps.body: A conditional split sends confirmed and cancelled down different paths: tag and dispatch on one, cancel and notify on the other.
steps.note: On Launch, skip the branch and handle non-responders from the Orders screen instead.

steps.title: Add a follow-up for silence
steps.body: Add a second wait of a few hours, then one more message. Stop there, because more than two asks reads as harassment.

steps.title: Publish and place a test COD order
steps.body: Use your own phone: tap Confirm and check the order records it. Then place another and tap Cancel.

blocks.text: Offering the prepaid switch
The strongest version of this flow offers to convert, not just confirm. A small incentive to pay now turns your riskiest orders into your safest, because prepaid orders almost never return to origin.

blocks.caption: Shopify voids the COD order and creates a paid one, so expect two order records for one purchase.

blocks.title: Two order records, one sale
blocks.body: A converted order appears twice in Shopify: the voided COD order and the new paid one. TopEdge recognises the replacement, so it is not counted twice against your order allowance, in revenue attribution, or in your COD share.

rows: Enough to beat the customer’s inertia, well below your RTO cost per order. Free shipping or a small flat discount is typical.
In the confirmation message itself, as the alternative to confirming COD. A separate later message converts far less.
What happens to the COD order
It is voided when the payment succeeds. The new paid order carries a tag identifying it as a conversion.
Nothing breaks. The original COD order stands and your normal flow continues.

A prepaid test order does **not** receive the confirmation.
Tapping Confirm is recorded against the order.
Tapping Cancel routes down the cancel path, if you built one.
A prepaid payment link opens a valid Shopify checkout for the right amount.

fixes: Add the **payment method = COD** filter to the trigger. Without it, order placed matches every order.
Republish after editing the trigger — a live journey keeps the trigger it was published with.

fixes: The template must use quick-reply buttons, not a URL button.
Send a test message first: if it reaches Live Chat, button taps will reach TopEdge too.

fixes: It is a Growth-and-above feature. See [plan limits](/docs/platform/limits-and-quotas).
Already-published journeys keep running after a downgrade, but you cannot edit or create them.

cases.symptom: A converted order looks like two orders
fixes: That is Shopify’s behaviour — the COD order is voided and a paid one created.
TopEdge skips the replacement for order counting, revenue and re-enrolment, so you are not billed or messaged twice.
If a replacement did get a second message, the conversion tag was stripped from the order in Shopify.

articles.title: Send Shopify order updates on WhatsApp
articles.description: Automate order confirmed, shipped, out for delivery and delivered messages on WhatsApp, and understand which Shopify event maps to which journey trigger.
articles.lead: The safest automation to start with: transactional, expected and no marketing consent needed. It also removes most "where is my order" messages before they are sent.

faqs.question: Which trigger should I use for a Shopify order confirmation?
faqs.answer: The order placed trigger. An order being placed is the confirmation event, and there is no separate order confirmed trigger. Expecting one is the most common reason a confirmation journey is built but never fires.

faqs.question: Do order status messages need marketing opt-in?
faqs.answer: No. They are transactional and send as Utility templates, which do not require marketing consent. That is exactly why they are the safest automation to start with — but it also means they must contain no promotional language at all.

faqs.question: Why are my shipped and delivered messages not sending?
faqs.answer: Almost always missing fulfilment permissions on the Shopify connection. Order confirmations only need order access, so confirmations keep working while shipping messages silently do nothing. Reconnect Shopify and approve the full permission list.

blocks.text: Publish one journey per stage (order placed, shipped, delivered), each sending an approved Utility template with an image header and tracking button. Shopify order and fulfilment webhooks fire the triggers. A status change you make in the dashboard enrols the journey directly, without waiting for Shopify.

fixes: The journey uses the **order placed** trigger — there is no order confirmed trigger.
The journey is Published, not Draft.
The template shows Approved, and the order has a phone number in international format.

fixes: Fulfilment permissions are missing. Settings → Shopify → **Reconnect** and approve everything.

fixes: Variables are unmapped on the node — open it and map each one to an order field.

articles.lead: Journeys message customers when something happens in Shopify. Flows decide what happens when a customer messages **you**, and without a published flow every inbound message waits for a human.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Flow Builder and Journeys?
faqs.answer: Flow Builder handles inbound conversations — what the bot says when a customer messages you, including menus, FAQ answers and handover to an agent. Journeys handle outbound automation triggered by Shopify events such as an order being placed or a cart being abandoned.

faqs.question: How many buttons can a WhatsApp message have?
faqs.answer: Three quick-reply buttons per message. If you need more options, use a list node instead, which presents up to ten rows behind a single tap and reads better than two stacked button messages.

faqs.question: Why does my flow still show the old menu after I edited it?
faqs.answer: Because the live bot runs a snapshot frozen at publish time. Saving the canvas updates the draft only. Publish again to replace the live graph, which takes effect from the next inbound message.

blocks.text: Open Flow Builder and start from the seeded welcome flow. articles.title: Send a WhatsApp broadcast that is Meta-safe
articles.description: Send a promotional WhatsApp broadcast to a consented segment: pick the audience, use an approved Marketing template, pass preflight, and read the results.
articles.lead: Broadcasts are the easiest thing in the product to get wrong, because the damage is not immediate. A bad send does not bounce; it quietly lowers your quality rating and messaging limit.

faqs.question: Do I need opt-in to send a WhatsApp broadcast?
faqs.answer: Yes. Promotional broadcasts use Marketing templates and require recorded consent from each contact. Transactional order updates are different — they send as Utility templates through journeys and do not need marketing consent.

faqs.question: Why was my broadcast blocked before sending?
faqs.answer: Preflight blocks a launch when too large a share of the audience has no recorded consent or has opted out. Fix the audience rather than the check: narrow to a consented segment, and remove any list you cannot prove consent for.

faqs.question: How many WhatsApp broadcasts can I send?
faqs.answer: Two separate limits apply. Your TopEdge plan caps campaign and email sends per billing cycle, and Meta caps how many unique customers you can start conversations with in 24 hours based on your quality rating and business verification.

blocks.text: Build a segment of contacts with recorded marketing consent and pick an approved **Marketing** template. articles.title: Run a shared WhatsApp inbox with your team
articles.description: Work a shared WhatsApp inbox: take a conversation over from the bot, reply inside and outside the 24-hour window, assign to a teammate and release it back.
articles.lead: Automation handles the predictable questions, and the inbox handles everything else. The handover between the two is where most teams lose conversations.

faqs.question: Why can I not send a free-form WhatsApp reply?
faqs.answer: The customer has not messaged you in the last 24 hours, so the service window has closed. WhatsApp only allows approved templates outside that window. Once the customer replies to your template, free text works again for another 24 hours.

faqs.question: What happens to the bot when an agent takes over?
faqs.answer: It pauses for that conversation only, and other conversations keep running their flows. It stays paused until someone presses **Give back to bot** or **Mark as done**, which is why a thread that seems permanently silent is usually still paused.

faqs.question: Can several agents work the same WhatsApp number?
faqs.answer: Yes. That is the point of a shared inbox — one business number, many agents, with assignment so two people do not answer the same customer. Each reply is attributed to the agent who sent it.

blocks.text: Open a conversation in Live Chat and press **Reply myself**; the bot pauses so only your team replies. articles.title: Collect WhatsApp opt-in on your storefront
articles.description: Add a popup, spin wheel or WhatsApp widget to your Shopify store, write consent wording that holds up, and confirm leads land in Audience.
articles.lead: Every promotional message you send depends on consent. It is not a checkbox to add later; it decides how large your sendable audience is a year from now.

faqs.question: What counts as valid WhatsApp marketing opt-in?
faqs.answer: A clear, affirmative action by the customer, with wording beside it that names WhatsApp marketing from your store specifically. A pre-ticked box, a buried line in your terms, or a list you bought do not count, and relying on them puts your business number at risk.

faqs.question: Why is my opt-in popup not showing on my Shopify store?
faqs.answer: In order of likelihood: the tool is still a draft, the TopEdge app embed is not enabled on your live theme, an ad blocker is hiding it, or your display rules exclude the page you are testing on. Test in an incognito window with blockers off.

faqs.question: Do customers have to opt in again to receive order updates?
faqs.answer: No. Order, shipping and delivery updates are transactional and send as Utility templates, which do not require marketing consent. Opt-in governs promotional broadcasts only, and opting out of marketing does not stop order updates.

blocks.text: Create a popup, spin wheel or WhatsApp widget in **Opt-in tools**, with consent wording that names WhatsApp marketing. Publish it, then enable the TopEdge opt-in app embed on your **live** Shopify theme. Each submission lands in Audience with its consent source recorded.

blocks.body: A customer who starts the chat gives you the strongest signal, and their first message opens the 24-hour window. Nobody has to dismiss it, so it never annoys anyone.

articles.title: Train the AI to answer customer questions
articles.description: Add your own AI key, load store knowledge, train intents on real customer phrases, and test confidence before letting the AI reply to customers.
articles.lead: A menu answers the questions you predicted. The AI brain answers the ones you did not — but only as well as the knowledge and the example phrases you give it.

faqs.question: Do I need my own OpenAI or Gemini key?
faqs.answer: For AI-generated replies, yes. TopEdge uses your own key, so usage is billed to you by that provider and you keep control of which model answers your customers. Keyword-matched intents with fixed replies work without any key.

faqs.question: How many example phrases does an intent need?
faqs.answer: Five to ten, taken from real customer messages rather than written by you. Phrases in your own phrasing score poorly because customers do not write like the person who built the store — expect Hinglish, abbreviations and no punctuation.

faqs.question: Should the AI handle refunds and complaints?
faqs.answer: No. Route anything involving money, a complaint or a legal question to a human. A confidently wrong answer about a refund costs far more than the time it saved, and customers escalate it publicly.

blocks.text: Add your own Gemini or OpenAI key and fill in store knowledge: shipping, returns, sizing and payment. Then create intents with five to ten phrases each, written the way customers actually type. Test each intent's confidence and activate it, because an inactive intent never matches.

items: WhatsApp connected, for live replies.
A Gemini or OpenAI API key. Keyword-only intents work without one.
A published flow as the fallback router — [Build your first flow](/docs/guides/build-your-first-flow).
Fifty real inbound messages to read before you start writing phrases.

blocks.title: You bring your own key
blocks.body: The AI runs on your own Gemini or OpenAI key, so the provider bills you for usage and you are not locked to a model TopEdge picked. Add it under **Intelligence → AI**.

blocks.text: Step 1 — load the knowledge

blocks.alt: Intelligence → AI with the store knowledge fields for shipping, returns, payments and sizing

blocks.text: The AI cannot invent your return window, and it should not try. Fill in store knowledge before any intent work, because it grounds every generated answer.

items: **Shipping** — dispatch time, delivery time by region, courier partners, what happens to a delayed order.
**Returns and exchanges** — the window, the condition requirement, who pays return shipping, how refunds are issued.
**Payments** — which methods you accept, whether COD is available and where, any COD fee.
**Sizing and product care** — the questions your category always gets.
**What you do not do** — no international shipping, no exchanges on sale items. Knowing the limits stops invented answers.

blocks.text: Step 2 — set the persona
**Intelligence → AI → Bot personality** sets the assistant’s name and tone. Keep it plain and close to how your brand already writes.
A wacky persona ages badly and makes complaints read worse than they are.
Step 3 — train intents on real phrases

blocks.alt: Intelligence → Intents list with each intent's phrases and Active toggle

steps.title: Read your inbox first
steps.body: Open the last fifty inbound messages and group them. The groups are your intents; the messages are your phrases.

steps.title: Create the intent
steps.body: **Intelligence → Intents → Add intent**. Name it for the question, such as "Shipping time".

steps.title: Add five to ten real phrases
steps.body: Copy how customers actually write: Hinglish, abbreviations, typos, no punctuation. "kitne din me ayega" trains better than "What is your delivery time?".
steps.note: Phrases you invented yourself are the main cause of low confidence scores.

steps.title: Choose what it does
steps.body: Reply with text, start a flow, assign to an agent, or escalate. Route asks like "I want a refund" to a human, not the AI.

steps.title: Activate it
steps.body: Toggle **Active**. An inactive intent never matches in production, however well trained.

steps.title: Test it
steps.body: Type sample messages into the test tool and read the matched intent and its confidence. Low or wrong matches need more phrases, or a split intent.

blocks.caption: Reading the test results
rows: Add three to five more phrases closer to how the message was worded.
Two intents are competing. Split them into narrower ones, or deactivate the duplicate.
Expected for genuinely new questions. Make sure your flow fallback hands these to a human.

blocks.title: Escalation is a feature, not a failure
blocks.body: The most damaging AI reply is a confident wrong one about a refund or a delivery date. Route money, complaints and anything legal to a human by design.

items: Your AI key is saved and the knowledge tabs accept input.
The test tool matches your sample phrases to the right intents.
Each intent you want live is toggled **Active**.
A real inbound message gets an AI reply when the bot is not paused on that thread.
An escalation intent puts the thread in the agent queue.

blocks.text: If the AI answers badly

cases.symptom: Test matches the wrong intent or reports low confidence
fixes: Add three to five more phrases in customers’ own words.
Split broad intents — "Shipping" and "Returns" should not be one intent.
Deactivate duplicate intents competing for the same phrases.

cases.symptom: The AI answers but the facts are wrong
fixes: Fill the gap in store knowledge — an empty field is where invention happens.
Add the limits explicitly, including what you do **not** offer.
Change that intent to a fixed reply instead of a generated one.

cases.symptom: The AI never replies at all
fixes: Check the intents are Active.
Check no agent pressed **Reply myself** on the thread in Live Chat.
Confirm your AI key is saved and valid with its provider.
Confirm a flow is Published as the fallback router.

articles.title: Run digital warranty registration on WhatsApp
articles.description: Set up warranty batches, share a mobile registration portal with WhatsApp OTP, and move claims through approved, shipped or rejected with automatic updates.
articles.lead: A warranty card in the box is a dead end: nobody posts it and you learn nothing. A QR on the packaging that opens WhatsApp registration gives you a verified contact and a reason to talk again.

faqs.question: How do customers register a warranty?
faqs.answer: They open your public registration portal — usually by scanning a QR on the packaging — select their product, enter their phone number and verify it with a WhatsApp OTP. The registration is then matched against the Shopify order where one exists.

faqs.question: Do customers need an account to claim?
faqs.answer: No. Registration and claims both work from a mobile web page with WhatsApp OTP verification, so there is no password and no app to install. That is deliberate — every extra step loses registrations.

blocks.text: Create a warranty batch linking Shopify products to coverage dates, then share the public registration portal, where customers verify by WhatsApp OTP. Work claims through pending, approved, shipped or rejected. Each status change sends the customer a WhatsApp update automatically.

articles.title: Segment Shopify customers for WhatsApp
articles.description: Build dynamic customer segments from order history, spend, tags and consent, then launch a WhatsApp or email campaign straight from the segment.
articles.lead: Sending to everyone is the most expensive habit in WhatsApp marketing: it costs you per message and in account health. A segment spends both on the people likely to buy.

faqs.question: Are TopEdge segments dynamic or a fixed list?
faqs.answer: Dynamic. A saved segment re-evaluates its conditions, so contacts move in and out as they order, lapse or change consent. You build a segment like "lapsed 90 days" once and it stays correct without any maintenance.

faqs.question: Why does my segment match zero customers?
faqs.answer: Conditions combine with AND, so every rule has to be true at once. Two reasonable-looking rules — say, more than three orders and ordered in the last seven days — can easily describe nobody. Add conditions one at a time and watch the live count.

blocks.text: Build a segment in **Audience → Segments** by stacking conditions on order count, spend, tags, consent and recency, and watch the live matching count. Save it, then press **Launch campaign** to open the broadcast builder with that audience selected.

items: Shopify connected, so order history and spend are populated.
Contacts in Audience — from [opt-in tools](/docs/guides/website-opt-in), checkout consent or orders.
Marketing consent recorded, if the segment will receive promotional messages.

blocks.text: Segments worth building first

rows: Cross-sell the obvious companion product, or ask for a review.
Two or more orders, consent recorded
Early access and restocks. This is your most valuable list.
A genuine reason to come back. This is where a discount earns its keep.
Treat differently — human outreach often beats a broadcast here.
Safe to push harder. These customers never cost you RTO.
Nothing promotional. Consider requiring prepayment instead.

steps.title: Open the segment builder

steps.title: Stack your conditions
steps.body: Add conditions on order count, total spend, tags, consent, days since last purchase or RTO count. They combine with AND.
steps.note: Because it is AND, three conditions can easily match nobody. Add one at a time and watch the count.

steps.title: Watch the matching count
steps.body: It updates as you edit. Zero means your conditions are too strict, so remove the last one you added.

steps.body: Without a consent condition, campaign preflight trims the audience anyway. Adding it here makes the count you see the count that sends.

steps.title: Save it
steps.body: Saved segments are dynamic: contacts move in and out as their behaviour changes. You never rebuild them.

steps.title: Launch a campaign from it
steps.body: Press **Launch campaign** to open the broadcast builder with this audience selected. See [Send a broadcast](/docs/guides/whatsapp-broadcast).

Lead scores rank contacts by engagement, not purchases, using waterfall rules you define. They surface contacts who opted in and browsed but never ordered, a group order-history segments cannot see.

blocks.title: Phone numbers match with or without the country code
blocks.body: Audience search handles Indian numbers both ways, so you do not have to guess the format a contact was saved in. Messages still send in full international format.

Add a consent condition to the segment so the two counts agree.

fixes: Search by their number both with and without the country code.

If they just opted in, allow a minute or two and refresh.

articles.title: Journeys reference: triggers, nodes, publishing
articles.description: Complete reference for TopEdge Journeys — every trigger type, trigger filter, node type, wait behaviour, publishing rule and revenue attribution window.
articles.lead: Journeys are visual automations that run when something happens in Shopify. You design a graph and publish it, and TopEdge turns it into timed steps for each customer who enters.

faqs.question: Why is my published journey not sending?
faqs.answer: Check in this order: the journey is Published rather than Draft, the template it uses is Approved right now, trigger filters do not exclude the customer, and the customer has a phone number. The order detail page records a skip reason naming the exact cause.

faqs.question: Do trigger filters combine with AND or OR?
faqs.answer: Always AND. Every active rule must be true for a customer to enter. This is why two reasonable-looking filters can exclude everybody — a minimum order value plus a specific product is a much narrower audience than it appears.

faqs.question: How is recovered revenue attributed to a journey?
faqs.answer: Last touch within seven days. If a journey message was the most recent TopEdge touch before the order, that journey is credited. The customer does not have to click the link, which avoids under-counting people who get the reminder and then visit your site directly.

blocks.text: A journey has one trigger, optional filters and a graph of nodes. Publishing freezes the graph and trigger, so edits change nothing until you publish again. Each enrolled customer gets their own timeline of scheduled steps, and by default a reply cancels the rest.
How a journey runs

blocks.name: journey-runtime
blocks.title: From Shopify event to sent message
blocks.caption: When a send does not happen, the skip reason on the order names which stage stopped it.

blocks.title: Publishing is what makes a journey live
blocks.body: Saving stores a draft; publishing snapshots the graph **and** the trigger. If you change the trigger in the editor, the journey keeps firing on the old one until you publish again.

blocks.text: Trigger types

rows: An order is created in Shopify. This is also your order-confirmation trigger.
An order is fulfilled, or a fulfilment updates with a non-delivered status.
A fulfilment updates with a delivered shipment status.
A checkout is abandoned and the capture delay has elapsed.
Nothing automatic — you enrol customers yourself from a list.

blocks.title: There is no "order confirmed" trigger
blocks.body: An order being placed *is* the confirmation. Hunting for a separate confirmed trigger is the most common reason a confirmation journey never fires.

blocks.text: Exit conditions
Exit conditions cancel a customer’s remaining steps.

items: **Customer replies**: available on every trigger and on by default, so a customer who already answered is not chased.
**Order cancelled**: available on order triggers.

blocks.text: Trigger filters
Filters decide who enters. **Every active rule must be true**: they combine with AND, never OR.
An empty rule set matches everything, which is usually right for an order-confirmation journey.

blocks.caption: Filters on order triggers
rows: Any, COD, or prepaid. This is how you build a COD-only journey.
Minimum, maximum, or both, in rupees.
Include or exclude specific Shopify products.
Indian states from a list, or a city as free text.
Whether a specific code was used.

blocks.caption: Filters on the cart abandoned trigger
rows: How long after abandonment the customer enters — 25 minutes by default.
Skip low-value carts that are not worth a conversation fee.

blocks.text: Node types

blocks.alt: Cart recovery journey on the canvas: entry node, three cart-recovery sends and the wait nodes between them

rows: The root of every journey. Holds the trigger, its filters and exit conditions. Cannot be deleted.
Sends an approved template with variables mapped from the order or cart.
Sends an email from your connected mailbox, with subject and body.
Sends the lifecycle template for a stage — confirmed, shipped, out for delivery or delivered.
A cart reminder with the live product image and a link back to checkout. Can also send a matching email.
Creates a Shopify draft invoice and injects the payment link into the message.
Delays the **next** sending node. Presets from 15 minutes to 7 days.
Two outputs, yes and no, based on a rule. Both branches must be wired before publish.
Hands the customer to a published flow, using the latest published version at send time.

blocks.text: How waits actually work
A wait node is not a step of its own. Its delay is added to the next node that sends something.

items: **Two waits in a row** add up.
**A wait at the end of a branch** does nothing.

blocks.text: Playbooks

blocks.alt: Journeys hub listing playbooks and live journeys for order and cart events

blocks.text: Journeys ships pre-built playbooks, so you never start from an empty canvas. Each has the right trigger and nodes in place; you map your approved templates and publish.
Runtime limits worth knowing

items.definition: A customer can be enrolled in at most two running automations at once. A third enrolment is skipped rather than queued, which stops a customer receiving four unrelated ladders at the same time.
On by default. A customer who answers your first message does not receive the rest of the ladder. You can turn it off on the entry node, but you usually should not.
An order is credited to the most recent journey touch within the previous 168 hours. The customer does not need to click your link for it to count.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a campaign and a journey?
faqs.answer: A campaign is a one-time send you decide to make, to an audience you pick, now or at a scheduled time. A journey is automation that runs whenever a Shopify event happens, for as long as it is published, without you touching it again.

faqs.question: Can one campaign send on both WhatsApp and email?
faqs.answer: No, one channel per campaign. To cover both, create two campaigns and keep the audiences from overlapping, so the same customer does not get the same message twice on two channels within minutes.

blocks.text: A campaign is one channel, one audience and one template. Preflight checks consent and template readiness before anything sends. Sends are batched and paced, not fired at once, so your WhatsApp quality rating survives the campaign.

**Preflight runs before launch, and it can block it.**

faqs.question: What is the WhatsApp 24-hour rule?
faqs.answer: When a customer messages your business, you get a 24-hour window in which you can reply with any kind of message. After 24 hours without a new message from them, only pre-approved templates will send. Their next message reopens the window for another 24 hours.

faqs.question: Does sending a template extend the 24-hour window?
faqs.answer: No. Only an inbound message from the customer resets the clock. But if the customer replies to your template, including by tapping a quick-reply button, a fresh 24-hour window opens.

faqs.question: Can I send a photo to a customer after 24 hours?
faqs.answer: Not as a free-form message. Outside the window only approved templates send, and a template can carry an image header. Once the customer replies you are back inside the window and can send media freely.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a Utility and a Marketing WhatsApp template?
faqs.answer: Utility templates are transactional updates about something the customer already did, such as an order confirmation, and need no marketing consent. Marketing templates are promotional and require recorded consent. Meta assigns the final category at review, so promotional wording in a Utility template is rejected.

faqs.question: Why does Meta keep rejecting my WhatsApp template?
faqs.answer: The most common cause is promotional language in a template submitted as Utility. blocks.text: Meta messaging limits
Separately from your plan, Meta limits how many unique customers you can send template messages to in a rolling 24 hours.
New accounts start low and rise with good-quality volume and business verification. Replies inside the [24-hour window](/docs/platform/whatsapp-service-window) don’t count.

rows: Customers blocking or reporting your messages
A sudden spike in volume from a cold list
Messaging contacts who never opted in
A healthy quality rating over time
Promotional content sent as Utility templates

blocks.text: Quality rating
Meta rates your number’s quality from how customers react. A low rating cuts your messaging limit and, at worst, restricts the number.
**Protect it.** A restricted business number costs far more than any campaign it carried.

blocks.title: Grow volume, do not jump to it
blocks.body: New to broadcasts? Send to your most engaged segment first and let the limit rise. Blasting a full list on day one is the fastest route to a restriction.

blocks.text: Automation runtime limits

rows: Stops one customer receiving four unrelated ladders at once. A third enrolment is skipped, not queued.
On by default. A customer who answered should not keep being chased.
Orders are credited to the last touch within 168 hours.

blocks.text: How hitting a limit shows up

cases.symptom: Messages stopped sending part-way through a campaign
fixes: Check your cycle send allowance in Settings → Billing.
Check your Meta messaging limit in Meta Business Manager.
A campaign row showing a partial send with no failures is almost always a cap.

cases.symptom: Orders stopped appearing
fixes: The order cap for the cycle may be reached — check usage in Billing.
Orders keep arriving in Shopify regardless; the automation stops, not your store.

cases.symptom: A journey node is locked
fixes: Branching and COD → prepaid need Growth or above.
Already-published journeys keep running; you cannot edit them until you upgrade.

articles.title: Troubleshooting WhatsApp automation
articles.description: Find your symptom and its fix — messages not sending, empty inbox, templates rejected, carts without phone numbers, broadcasts blocked and connection errors.
articles.lead: Organised by what you see, not by which part of the product is at fault. Find your symptom and work the fixes in order; the most likely comes first.

faqs.question: Why is my WhatsApp automation not sending messages?
faqs.answer: In order of likelihood: the journey is still in Draft rather than Published, the template it uses is not Approved at send time, trigger filters are excluding the customer, or the order has no phone number. The activity list on the affected order records a skip reason naming the actual cause.

faqs.question: Why is my WhatsApp inbox empty?
faqs.answer: Almost always because TopEdge isn't subscribed to your messages. Reconnect from Settings → WhatsApp to fix it. Sending works without it but nothing inbound arrives. Check the Webhook tab in WhatsApp settings, and test by messaging your business number from a personal phone.

faqs.question: Who do I contact for help with TopEdge?
faqs.answer: Use the contact page on this site. Include your store domain, what you expected, what actually happened, a screenshot of any banner, and the order number if it’s about a specific order. That usually gets a fix in one reply.

blocks.text: Most problems are one of four things: a journey left in Draft, a template not Approved at send time, TopEdge not receiving your messages, or storefront tracking not capturing a phone. Check those first, and read the skip reason on the affected order; it usually names the cause.

blocks.title: Start with the skip reason
blocks.body: If a customer missed a message about an order, open that order in [Orders](/docs/reference/orders). Its activity list shows what was tried and why it was skipped.

blocks.text: Nothing is sending

cases.symptom: A journey is live but customers get no messages
fixes: Confirm the journey shows **Published**, not Draft. Saving is not publishing.
Confirm every template it uses shows **Approved** right now — Meta can pause an approved template later.
Check trigger filters are not excluding the customer. Rules combine with AND.
Confirm the order or cart carries a phone number in international format.
Read the skip reason on the order — see [Orders](/docs/reference/orders#activity).

cases.symptom: Order confirmations never fire
fixes: The journey must use the **order placed** trigger. There is no "order confirmed" trigger.
Republish after changing a trigger — a live journey keeps the trigger it was published with.
See [Order status updates](/docs/guides/order-status-updates#triggers).

cases.symptom: Shipped and delivered never fire, but confirmations work
fixes: Fulfilment permissions are missing on the Shopify connection.
Settings → Shopify → **Reconnect** and approve the full permission list.
See [Connect Shopify](/docs/connect-shopify#permissions).

cases.symptom: Messages stopped part-way through a campaign
fixes: Check your cycle send allowance in Settings → Billing.
Check your Meta messaging limit in Meta Business Manager.
See [limits and quotas](/docs/platform/limits-and-quotas#what-it-looks-like).

blocks.text: The inbox is wrong

cases.symptom: Inbox is completely empty
fixes: TopEdge isn't receiving your messages (reconnect from Settings → WhatsApp). This is the single most common cause.
Message from a personal phone — a business number cannot message itself.
Confirm a flow is **Published** in Flow Builder.
See [Connect WhatsApp](/docs/connect-whatsapp#troubleshooting).

cases.symptom: Send button is greyed out or says the session expired
fixes: The 24-hour window has closed. Pick an approved template — see [the service window](/docs/platform/whatsapp-service-window).
WhatsApp may be disconnected. Reconnect in Settings.
A Marketing template to an opted-out contact is blocked by design.

cases.symptom: The bot replies while an agent is typing
fixes: Press **Reply myself** on the thread. That pauses the bot for this chat.
See [inbox and handover](/docs/guides/shared-inbox-handover#daily-work).

cases.symptom: The bot never replies again on one thread
fixes: The thread is still with an agent. Press **Give back to bot**.
**Mark as done** also hands the chat back to the bot.

blocks.text: Template problems

cases.symptom: Template is stuck Pending
fixes: Approval is usually minutes but can take up to 24 hours on a first submission.
Use **Sync from Meta** in Meta Manager if the status looks stale.

cases.symptom: Template was rejected
fixes: Read Meta’s reason on the template row.
Utility templates must contain no promotional words — sale, discount, offer, % off, free gift.
Do not start or end the body with a variable, and give realistic sample values.
See [message templates](/docs/platform/message-templates#rejection-reasons).

cases.symptom: Template library is empty
fixes: You are connected to a different WhatsApp Business Account than the one holding your templates.
Check which account the connection names, then reconnect to the right one.
Run **Sync from Meta** afterwards.

cases.symptom: A message arrived with blank values
fixes: Variables are unmapped on the journey node. Open it and map each one.
Or the field is genuinely empty on that record — a tracking number before dispatch, for example.
Preview against a real order rather than sample data.

cases.symptom: A template that used to work has stopped
fixes: Meta can pause an approved template if its quality drops.
Check template quality in Meta Business Manager and the skip reason on an affected order.

blocks.text: Cart recovery problems

cases.symptom: Abandoned carts list is empty
fixes: All three layers on Store growth → Website tracking must be green.
Enable the TopEdge app embed on the **live** theme, not a preview.
Test in incognito with ad blockers off.
On a third-party checkout, configure the partner webhook.
See [store growth](/docs/reference/store-growth#tracking).

cases.symptom: Carts appear but the phone column is blank
fixes: The customer left before a step that collects a phone number — normal for browse abandonment.
On a custom phone or OTP page, add `data-topedge-phone="true"` to the input.
See [abandoned cart recovery](/docs/guides/abandoned-cart-recovery#capture).

cases.symptom: Carts have phone numbers but no reminder sends
fixes: The cart journey is in Draft. Publish it.
All three cart templates should be Approved — one pending template stops the ladder part-way.
A minimum cart value filter may be excluding the cart.

cases.symptom: Recovered revenue stays at zero
fixes: Nobody has completed a checkout after receiving a reminder yet.
Attribution is last touch within seven days — later orders fall outside it.
Confirm your test order used the same phone number as the cart.

blocks.text: Broadcast problems

cases.symptom: Launch blocked — too many contacts opted out
fixes: Filter Audience by consent to see who is excluded.
Remove any purchased or scraped list — there is no safe way to send to one.
Narrow to a consented segment and send to that.
See [send a broadcast](/docs/guides/whatsapp-broadcast#troubleshooting).

cases.symptom: The template you want is not in the picker
fixes: Broadcasts need the **Marketing** category. Utility templates are not offered.
It may still be pending approval.

cases.symptom: Delivered is far below sent
fixes: Invalid numbers or numbers not on WhatsApp — clean the list.
Some recipients have blocked your business number.
If it is widespread, check your quality rating in Meta Business Manager.

blocks.text: Connection problems

blocks.alt: Settings channels showing WhatsApp and Shopify connection status

cases.symptom: Amber "WhatsApp disconnected" bar on every page
fixes: Reconnect in Settings → WhatsApp.
Using manual credentials? Paste a fresh permanent System User token. A channel that dies after a day was on a 24-hour test token.
Confirm the number has not been migrated or disconnected inside Meta Business Manager.

cases.symptom: Shopify shows Reconnect
fixes: Approve the full permission list again. Until you do, features relying on new permissions silently do nothing.
Then open Orders → **Sync**.

cases.symptom: Embedded signup says the phone number is already in use
fixes: The number is registered in the WhatsApp Business app. Delete that account or enable coexistence.
Check for another Cloud API app claiming the number in Meta Business Manager.

cases.symptom: Everything is connected but hubs are empty
fixes: Press **Sync** on Orders — the first load is a backfill, not a webhook.
Reload the dashboard; connection state is cached briefly.
Confirm the connected store is the one you are looking at in Shopify admin.

cases.symptom: Hubs show data with a "Sample data" pill
fixes: That’s the labelled sample preview, shown until a channel is connected. It isn’t your store’s data.
Connect WhatsApp and Shopify in Settings to switch to live data.
Actions in sample mode never send and never report success.

blocks.text: Opt-in tool problems

cases.symptom: Popup or widget never shows
fixes: Status must be **Published**, not Draft.
Enable the TopEdge Opt-In app embed on the **live** theme and Save.
Test in incognito with ad blockers disabled, and hard-refresh.
Loosen the display rules — a strict URL or device rule may exclude your test page.
See [collect opt-in](/docs/guides/website-opt-in#troubleshooting).

cases.symptom: Submission works but the contact is not in Audience
fixes: Search by the exact number, with and without the country code.
Wait a minute or two and refresh.
Confirm the tool is Published — a draft can preview without recording anything.

blocks.text: Still stuck
Contact us through [the contact page](/contact). For a useful answer first time, include:

items: Your **store domain**.
What you expected to happen, and what happened instead.
A screenshot of any banner or error.
The order number, if it’s about a specific order or cart.
